prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a sideswipe while changing lanes in Houston, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1482; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my name on the recording, if that's okay. You already have it on the claim.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where the accident happened?
A: It was on a multi-lane highway in Houston, Texas, heading into the city during the commute. I was in the right lane.
Q: What were you doing right before the collision?
A: I was changing lanes to move over for an exit. I checked my mirror, saw the lane looked clear, and started to merge.
Q: What happened next?
A: The other vehicle was in my blind spot. It sideswiped the driver's side of my car. There was a loud scraping sound and my car pulled toward the shoulder.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: Not clearly. I didn't see it until it was already next to me.
Q: Did you stop at the scene?
A: Yes, I pulled onto the shoulder and stayed in the car until the officer arrived. He took information from both drivers.
Q: Where are you feeling injuries now?
A: My neck is stiff and sore, especially when I turn my head to the left. My lower back aches too, and it's worse when I sit for a long time.
Q: Have you seen a doctor or received any treatment?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic the same day. They said it looked like a neck and back strain. I've been doing physical therapy twice a week since then.
Q: Is there anything else you would like to add?
A: Only that I'm trying to get back to normal and I want the claim handled quickly so I can keep up with my bills while I recover.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
A: Thank you.
